It buzzed loudly for ten days, shook across my counter, and died.

Then came my routine dental cleaning.

I sat in the chair and half-apologized for what I thought was a little coffee stain.

My dentist scraped along my gumline with her metal probe.

She stopped and sighed.

I had two cavities.

And along the exact edge where the plastic tray rested, my enamel had chalky white spots.

Permanent demineralization.

The water was murky and brown.
